definition_zh: 候选人；申请人；应试者；有望成为……的人（或物）
definition_en: a person who applies for or is put forward for a job, office, honor, or degree; also a thing likely to undergo or suit something
core_image: 古罗马候选人穿一袭特别亮的白袍走在广场上，让人一眼认出他在谋求职位
scene: 招聘会现场，简历一份份递进摊位，玻璃门后是面试官的长桌。Each candidate gave a five-minute self-introduction before the panel.
sceneCN: 这里 candidate 是「求职者、应聘者」（第 2 个义项：谋求职位而接受考察的人）；句意是每位应聘者都向评审团做了五分钟的自我介绍。

pos.zh: 有望成为……的人（或物）；适合的目标

derivatives.zh: 由 candidate 加抽象后缀构成，义为「候选资格；候选期」
同根词，义为「坦率的；直白的」（同出拉丁语 candidus）
同源远亲，义为「蜡烛」（源自「发光、白亮」同一词根）

senses.title: A person standing for election
senses.definition: a person formally put forward to compete for an elected office
senses.definitionCN: 被正式提名参加竞选公职的人
senses.example: Three candidates are competing for the mayoral seat.
senses.exampleCN: 三名候选人正在角逐市长职位。
senses.why: The Roman office-seeker wore a whitened toga, candidatus, to stand out in the forum.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的谋官者身穿漂白托加袍（candidatus），好在广场上引人注目。

senses.title: An applicant for a job or position
senses.definition: a person being considered for a post, especially through interviews or review
senses.definitionCN: 正被考虑录用的人选，通常经过面试或评审
senses.example: The committee interviewed twelve candidates for the professorship.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会面试了十二位申请该教席的人。
senses.why: Interviewing is the modern forum: applicants still present themselves to be seen and judged.
senses.whyCN: 面试就是现代的广场：申请人依然要亮相、被观看与评判。

senses.title: A person taking an examination
senses.definition: a person sitting an examination or seeking an academic degree
senses.definitionCN: 参加考试或谋求学位的人
senses.example: Candidates must present their identification before entering the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 考生进入考场前须出示身份证件。
senses.why: A degree candidate stands for a honor yet to be conferred, an unfinished candidacy.
senses.whyCN: 学位候选人谋求的是尚未授予的资格，候选状态尚未完成。

senses.title: A thing likely to be chosen or affected
senses.definition: a person or thing considered likely to receive, undergo, or suit something
senses.definitionCN: 被认为很可能获得、经历或适合某事的人或物
senses.example: The old bridge is a candidate for demolition.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老桥很可能被拆除。
senses.why: Selection language transfers from people to objects: anything can wear the bright toga.
senses.whyCN: 遴选用语由人转移到物：任何对象都可能穿上那件亮白袍。

intro.en: Candidate comes from Latin candidatus, clothed in white, the shining toga worn by Roman office-seekers, from candidus, glowing white.
intro.cn: candidate 源自拉丁语 candidatus（穿白衣的），即罗马谋官者所穿的亮白托加袍，词根是 candidus（发亮的白色）。

items.en: The root *kand- means to shine or glow, giving words for light and whiteness.
items.cn: 词根 *kand- 意为发光、白亮，衍生出一批关于光与白的词。

items.en: Latin candidus meant white, pure, or sincere; candidatus described the bleached toga of an office-seeker.
items.cn: 拉丁语 candidus 意为白的、纯洁的、真诚的；candidatus 形容谋官者漂白的托加袍。

items.en: In the forum, the bright toga made the seeker instantly visible; hence candidatus became the word for an office-seeker.
items.cn: 在广场上，亮白袍让谋求职位者一眼可辨，candidatus 因此成为「谋官者」的专称。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the seventeenth century, at first with a Roman flavor, then for any aspirant.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入该词，起初带着罗马色彩，随后泛指一切谋求者。

items.en: Today it covers politicians, job applicants, examinees, and even objects slated for action.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖政客、求职者、考生，甚至被列入处理名单的物品。

note.en: Candidate anchors the candidus family of whiteness and openness, and sits beside words for hopeful entrants.
note.cn: candidate 是 candidus「白亮、坦诚」词族的核心，并与一系列「谋求者」词汇相邻。

entries.definition: Frank and straightforward, from the same white-pure root.
entries.definitionCN: 坦率的，源自同一「纯白」词根。

entries.definition: The state or period of being a candidate.
A wax light, from the same shining root via Latin candela.
entries.definitionCN: 蜡烛，经拉丁语 candela 出自同一「发光」词根的远亲。

entries.definition: Glowing with heat, the shining root with the in- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 白热的；炽热的，同一发光词根加前缀 in- 构成。

entries.definition: One who formally applies, especially in writing.
One formally named for an office or honor.
One who competes seriously for something contested.
entries.definitionCN: 认真角逐竞争的争夺者。

entries.definition: One who ambitiously seeks a high position.
entries.definitionCN: 雄心勃勃谋求高位的人。

entries.definition: The current holder of the office a candidate seeks.
entries.definitionCN: 在任者，即候选人所谋求职位的现任持有者。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the white toga story and the shining root family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕「白袍典故」与「发光」词根家族的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root story: Roman office-seekers wore a bleached toga, candidatus, the man in white.
normal.cn: 词根典故：罗马谋官者身穿漂白托加袍，candidatus 即「白衣人」。

normal.en: Same root: candid, candor, candle, and incandescent all shine from one glowing stem.
normal.cn: 同根串联：candid、candor、candle、incandescent 都从同一「发光」词干发亮。

normal.en: Collocation grid: presidential candidate, doctoral candidate, a candidate for surgery cover politics, study, and medicine.
normal.cn: 搭配网格：presidential candidate、doctoral candidate、a candidate for surgery 分别对应政界、学界、医学。

normal.en: Opposite hook: the incumbent is already in the chair the candidate wants.
normal.cn: 反义钩子：incumbent（在任者）已坐上候选人想要的位子。

normal.en: Derived noun: candidacy names the campaign period itself, as in launch a candidacy.
normal.cn: 派生名词：candidacy 指候选期本身，如 launch a candidacy（宣布参选）。

abstract.en: A toga bleached so bright it blinds, worn straight into the crowd of voters.
abstract.cn: 一件白得晃眼的托加袍，径直穿进选民的人潮。

abstract.en: A row of chairs outside an interview room, each one holding a hopeful silhouette.
abstract.cn: 面试室外的一排椅子，每把椅子上都坐着一个满怀期待的剪影。

abstract.en: A single name underlined in bright chalk on the blackboard list.
abstract.cn: 黑板名单上一个用亮粉笔加下划线的名字。

examples.en: Every candidate promised to fix the same three potholes.
examples.cn: 每位候选人都承诺修好同样三个坑洼。

examples.en: The search firm narrowed the pool to six candidates.
examples.cn: 猎头公司把候选人范围缩小到六人。

examples.en: Doctors agreed he was an ideal candidate for the transplant.
examples.cn: 医生一致认为他是移植手术的理想人选。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坎地得」——翻过坎（坎）走到台前（地）才能得（得）到职位，谋求者先过坎再得地，正是候选人；联想罗马人穿白袍亮相互选。

root: 源自拉丁语 candidatus（身穿白衣者），指罗马共和国谋求公职者所穿的漂白托加袍；词根为 candidus（发亮的白色、纯洁），可上溯至印欧词根 *kand-（发光）。同根词有 candid（坦率的）、candor（坦诚）、candle（蜡烛）、incandescent（白热的）。十七世纪借入英语，词义从谋官者扩至一切谋求者与受考察者。

sensesIntro.en: From the man in the bright toga the word spreads to job applicants, examinees, and even objects awaiting action.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「穿亮袍的人」出发，词义扩展到求职者、考生，乃至等待处理的物品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in a shining white robe, standing out so the crowd can choose him.
core.cn: 核心意象：一身白袍亮到反光的人，站在人群中引人选择。

branches.en: THE FORUM: the Roman candidate turned modern politician.
branches.cn: 广场：从罗马谋官者到现代政客。

branches.en: THE INTERVIEW ROOM: applicants presenting themselves for judgment.
branches.cn: 面试间：接受评判的申请者。

branches.en: THE EXAM HALL: candidates seeking a degree or certificate.
branches.cn: 考场：谋求学位或证书的应试者。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: things shortlisted for repair, demolition, or study.
branches.cn: 工场：被列入待修、待拆、待研究名单的事物。

branches.en: THE COMMON THREAD: to be a candidate is to stand out and be chosen or refused.
branches.cn: 共同线索：身为候选人，就是要站出来被选中或被淘汰。

intro.en: Candidate is candidus plus the agentive ending -atus, the man made shining white.
intro.cn: candidate 由 candidus 加施动词尾 -atus 构成，即「被弄得雪亮白的人」。

latinIntro.en: The candidus root of shining white feeds a bright family from candles to incandescent bulbs.
latinIntro.cn: candidus「发光之白」词根滋养了一个从蜡烛到白炽灯泡的光亮词族。

items.meaning: the state of being a candidate

latinEntries.exampleCN: 执政官职位候选人（拉丁语用例示意）。
